event.title: A Worthy Objective: National Teachers Day at the Center
event.venue_json: {"id":266,"global_id":"www.civilandhumanrights.org?id=266","venue":"National Center for Civil and Human Rights","address":"100 Ivan Allen Jr. Blvd","city":"Atlanta","country":"United States","state":"GA","website":"civilandhumanrights.org","url":"https://www.civilandhumanrights.org/event-space/ncchr__trashed/","geo_lat":33.764055,"geo_lng":-84.3930512,"show_map":false,"show_map_link":false}
event.description: In honor of National Teachers Day, the Center invites educators to enjoy an afternoon of inspiration, exploration, and appreciation. Inspired by Dr. Martin Luther King Jr.’s belief that education should provide both “the power of concentration” and “worthy objectives on which to concentrate,” this special event offers teachers the opportunity to experience the Center at their own pace while discovering exhibitions, programs, and resources designed to support learning beyond the classroom. Throughout the afternoon, the Education Team will spotlight resources available to teachers through facilitated Field Guide experiences and Traveling Trunk demonstrations, providing ideas for bringing civil and human rights education into classrooms and learning spaces. Educators can also participate in art and history activities that celebrate the curiosity and creativity at the heart of great teaching. Whether you’re looking for classroom inspiration, educational tools, or simply an afternoon to explore, we invite you to celebrate the power of education at the Center.

event.description: Join us this Saturday for an unforgettable experience with interactive storyteller Mama Koku, who will lead high-energy, improvised storytelling sessions at 12 p.m. Known for her magnetic stage presence, Mama Koku transforms storytelling into “story-doing,” inviting children and families to step into the narrative and become part of the performance. Each session is lively, creative, and completely unique, blending imagination, movement, and collaboration in a way that keeps audiences fully engaged. While you’re here, be sure to explore Change Agent Adventure: Children’s Gallery, an interactive space designed for children 12 and under. This hands-on “secret headquarters” invites kids to play, create, and build confidence as they discover what it means to be a changemaker. About the Storyteller Mama Koku is a celebrated teaching artist and storyteller known throughout Metro Atlanta for her dynamic and interactive style. A graduate with honors from North Carolina Central University, she studied theater with concentrations in performance and education. She began her career as a high school theatre teacher, where she honed her work as a storyteller and children’s writer. Her engaging approach has earned her recognition as the Official Teller for the National Black Arts Festival’s Education Village and The Coretta Scott King Book Awards Book Fair. Website: Mama Koku | Watch the Stories Come to Life

event.title: CIVICS 4 ALL AGES!!

event.description: The fight for justice, equality, and civic participation belongs to all of us, and it is never too early to begin learning how to make a difference. CIVICS 4 ALL AGES! is a special family learning experience that helps participants better understand how government works, why civic engagement matters, and how individuals can create change in their communities. Through engaging discussions and real-world examples, families will explore the foundations of civics in a welcoming and accessible environment. Hosted in the Action Lab and Rotunda, the program is designed for both adults and young learners, with activities tailored to each audience. The experience begins with youth-focused programming that introduces civic concepts through interactive, kid-friendly activities before shifting to sessions designed for adults, allowing every family member to participate and learn. Whether you’re looking to build your civic knowledge, spark meaningful family conversations, or inspire the next generation of changemakers, CIVICS 4 ALL AGES! offers a unique opportunity for the whole family to learn, engage, and grow together.

event.title: National Buy Nothing Day at the Center
event.venue_json: {"id":266,"global_id":"www.civilandhumanrights.org?id=266","venue":"National Center for Civil and Human Rights","address":"100 Ivan Allen Jr. Blvd","city":"Atlanta","country":"United States","state":"GA","website":"civilandhumanrights.org","url":"https://www.civilandhumanrights.org/event-space/ncchr__trashed/","geo_lat":33.764055,"geo_lng":-84.3930512,"show_map":false,"show_map_link":false}
event.description: The day after Thanksgiving is often known as one of the biggest shopping days of the year, but National Buy Nothing Day invites us to pause and think differently about consumption, community, and the impact of our choices. Join the Center for an afternoon of learning and reflection as we explore how everyday purchasing decisions affect people, communities, and the environment. Through engaging activities and conversations, visitors will gain new perspectives on ethical consumption and discover ways to make more intentional choices. In partnership with the Atlanta Tool Bank, guests can participate in special “My Passion” sessions to learn about each organization’s mission and how they help build a more sustainable Atlanta. The event will also feature an ethical footprint-themed art activity, a live artist painting experience, and a donation collection that encourages giving back to the community. Whether you’re interested in reducing waste, rethinking consumer habits, or finding practical ways to make a positive impact, National Buy Nothing Day at the Center offers an inspiring opportunity to explore sustainability, stewardship, and community action.
